cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: Airport-bound traffic on Bellary Road faces 18 months of disruption from today; buses and goods vehicles are barred from the affected stretch.

lead.headline: 18-MONTH AIRPORT ROAD DISRUPTION BEGINS TODAY
lead.deck: Elevated-corridor work closes a key Ballari Road stretch to buses and goods vehicles; motorists must use diversions
paragraphs: Traffic restrictions begin Friday on Bengaluru’s Kempegowda International Airport Road as the Bangalore Development Authority starts a four-lane elevated corridor project along Ballari Road. The work is expected to disrupt traffic for 18 months.

KSRTC and private buses, along with all goods vehicles, are prohibited on the affected stretch between UAS Staff Quarters and Mekhri Circle. Traffic police have announced alternative routes for airport-bound and city-bound vehicles.

Travellers from Hebbal heading to the airport can divert via Old High Grounds, Cantonment railway station, Tannery Road and Nagawara Road. The change is likely to affect airport journeys and commuter traffic across north Bengaluru.

image.alt: Representational image accompanying the Bengaluru airport-road traffic advisory
image.caption: Representational image. Traffic restrictions on the airport road begin November 6.

sidebarStory.headline: BENGALURU TECHIE HELD OVER THREATS TO BOLLYWOOD ACTORS
sidebarStory.subhead: Police say the accused allegedly invoked a gang’s name to threaten Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor
paragraphs: Mumbai Police arrested a 30-year-old Bengaluru IT engineer over alleged threat messages to actors Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor. Police said the accused appeared to have impersonated a Lawrence Bishnoi gang associate but was not linked to the gang; officers suspect he may have used AI-generated voice samples.

image.alt: Actor Ayushmann Khurrana, who received an alleged threat call
image.caption: Ayushmann Khurrana had recently received an alleged threat call. Photo: Instagram

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru crime, transport, and household news

stories.headline: FACTORY OWNER HELD AFTER WORKER IS BEATEN TO DEATH
paragraphs: Police arrested a manufacturing-unit owner after a 24-year-old worker from Kerala was allegedly assaulted with a cricket bat and an iron pipe at a Yelahanka home. The killing followed a confrontation, police said; the worker’s family has alleged the attack was premeditated.

stories.headline: BELAGAVI SUGARCANE FARMERS END WEEK-LONG PROTEST
paragraphs: Sugarcane growers in Belagavi have called off their week-long agitation after mills agreed to pay ₹3,600 per tonne for the 2026–27 crushing season. The district arrangement also includes a share of additional proceeds if sugar sales generate higher earnings; farmers had sought a higher base price and state support.

stories.headline: NANDINI GHEE, BUTTER AND PANEER PRICES RISE
paragraphs: Revised prices for Nandini ghee, butter and paneer took effect across Karnataka on November 4, following recent milk and curd increases. A one-litre ghee sachet rose from ₹715 to ₹850 and a one-kilogram paneer pack from ₹408 to ₹485, adding pressure on household and food-business budgets.

groups.ariaLabel: India public safety, courts, and rural policy news

stories.headline: TWO DEAD AS UNDER-CONSTRUCTION BUILDING COLLAPSES IN OLD DELHI
paragraphs: A three-storey building under construction collapsed in the crowded Chawri Bazaar area on Thursday. Two people were confirmed dead and several others were feared trapped; rescue teams worked in narrow lanes where heavy machinery could not reach. Delhi authorities ordered two engineers suspended and an FIR against the contractor.

image.alt: Rescue teams work at the collapsed building site in Delhi’s Chawri Bazaar
image.caption: NDRF teams search the Chawri Bazaar collapse site. Source: ANI/PTI via The Indian Express

stories.headline: UMAR KHALID AND SHARJEEL IMAM MOVE SUPREME COURT FOR BAIL
paragraphs: The two activists have separately challenged the Delhi High Court’s rejection of their fresh bail pleas in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. Their petitions cite the length of pre-trial detention and the prosecution’s progress; the Supreme Court has yet to decide the appeals.

stories.headline: CENTRE IDENTIFIES 22 WORKS TO SUPPORT FODDER AND LIVESTOCK
paragraphs: The Centre has asked states and Union Territories to strengthen fodder security, pasture development and livestock infrastructure under the VB-G RAM G Act. The rural development ministry identified 22 permissible works, including measures to support livestock-based rural livelihoods.

groups.ariaLabel: Karnataka elections, environment, and governance news

stories.headline: STATE TO PROBE ALLEGED MISUSE OF FORM 7 VOTER APPLICATIONS
paragraphs: Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said Karnataka would launch a police investigation into alleged misuse of Form 7 applications, which can seek deletion of names from electoral rolls. He accused the BJP of trying to manipulate voter lists; the allegation has not been adjudicated.

stories.headline: PIL CHALLENGES MLA’S APPOINTMENT AS POLLUTION CONTROL BOARD CHAIR
paragraphs: The Karnataka High Court issued notices to the state government and Anekal MLA B Shivanna on a public-interest petition challenging his appointment as chairperson of the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board. The petition raises questions about eligibility for the role.

stories.headline: SC SENDS TMC PLEA ON 10 REBEL MLAS TO CALCUTTA HIGH COURT
paragraphs: The Supreme Court disposed of a TMC legislator’s plea seeking faster disqualification proceedings against 10 rebel MLAs, allowing him to approach the Calcutta High Court. The petition alleged delay by the state Assembly Speaker in deciding the cases.

groups.ariaLabel: India sport and Bengaluru weather news

stories.headline: INDIA BEAT JAPAN 4–1 TO WIN RECORD SIXTH ASIAN CHAMPIONS TROPHY
paragraphs: India came from a goal down to defeat Japan 4–1 in the final at Mohali, securing a record-extending sixth men’s Asian Champions Trophy. The win completed a third consecutive title for the defending champions.

stories.headline: IMD FORECASTS CLOUD AND LIGHT RAIN TODAY
paragraphs: The IMD expects generally cloudy skies and light rain in Bengaluru on Friday, with a thunderstorm accompanied by lightning in the warning. The city forecast gives a minimum of 20°C and a maximum of 30°C.
